subject: how to do single-species occupancy on different space and time dataset

messages.author: 73bd1ab0bc46b84f
messages.subject: how to do single-species occupancy on different space and time dataset
parts:
Hello everyone! I’m a graduate student planning to conduct research on how climate affects mammal distribution across a large area. I’ll be using camera trap data collected from multiple locations within the area of interest (AOI) (different space and time), with data collection spanning different periods (2015–2020).

Originally, I planned to use single-species occupancy in relation to environmental and climate variables. However, given the varied data collection periods, climatic conditions may also differ across locations. For instance, the extreme forest fires in 2015 may have significantly impacted the climate that year. 

My question is: Given the differences in climatic conditions in each period of camera trapping effort, how can I analyze all this data to produce a single distribution prediction? There may be inappropriate assumptions because climate is time-sensitive.

Are there alternative methods or models that could be effective for this kind of dataset?

Any insights or recommendations would be greatly appreciated!

messages.author: c1c42f596a4aec46
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] how to do single-species occupancy on different space and time dataset
parts:
Hi Irfan,

Can you clarify whether  you were planning to use a single season or dynamic occupancy model? It seems like based on what you've described, a dynamic occupancy model (colext in unmarked) would be a good fit.

-Reed
